claims.claim: Measured human em dash density (mean 3.23, range 0.33–17.12 per 1,000 words) envelops the LLM range (0.0–10.62 across twelve models), and the rate is a provider-specific fine-tuning artifact, with Llama's RLHF suppressing it to zero.
claims.source: arXiv 2603.27006 — E. M. Freeburg, The Last Fingerprint
claims.quote: a diagnostic signature of how a model was fine-tuned
claims.page: How Markdown Training Shapes LLM Prose

claims.claim: Readers who relied on em dashes to spot ChatGPT text performed only marginally better than chance, and no single lexical or punctuation feature is definitive.
claims.page: Spotting text written by ChatGPT is still more art than science

claims.claim: Heavy em dash use in contemporary fiction has been taught by New York editors since the 1990s, and the tells cited against Shy Girl (flat voice, improbable similes, em dashes) equally fit unedited, neurodivergent or ESL human writing.
claims.quote: also be attributed to amateurish or unedited writing
claims.page: Does the Shy Girl Mess Mean We Give Up the Em Dash?

claims.claim: Em dashes, serial commas and the rule of three are basic tenets of fiction that a human author can deploy in a single self-written sentence, so their presence is not evidence of generation.
claims.quote: touted as being 'clear indicators of AI usage'

claims.claim: The tricolon is a canonical human device — Caesar, Lincoln, Churchill, King, fairy tales, Aristotle's beginning-middle-end — because three is the smallest count that makes a pattern.
Craft guidance for novelists teaches deliberate use of triads (omne trium perfectum, Dickens' three spirits, three-act structure), with the only caution being restraint.
claims.source: Jericho Writers — Amy de la Force, 2022
claims.page: The Rule Of Three In Writing: Our Guide

claims.claim: A detector vendor concedes that LLM triads are a reflection of effective communication strategies in human training data and that professional writing employs the rule of three for clarity.
claims.quote: a reflection of effective communication strategies embedded within their training data
claims.page: How to Break Free from GPT's Rule of Three in Writing

claims.claim: Even a writer who calls 'It's not X; it's Y' the biggest ChatGPT tell concedes contrastive antithesis is concise, was stylish before saturation, and is failing as a fashion cycle rather than as a device.
claims.quote: contrastive antithesis is part of ChatGPT's lexicon for a reason.
claims.page: Some alternatives to "It's not X; it's Y"

claims.claim: Wikipedia's own AI-cleanup guide states parallel constructions are common among human writers (myth-busting listicles), that none of its signs prove AI authorship, and that human writing is converging on LLM style.
claims.quote: Not all text featuring these indicators is AI-generated

claims.claim: Wikipedia's guide warns that automated detectors have non-trivial error rates and cites a 2025 study finding human discrimination of LLM text no better than chance.
claims.quote: Human speech and writing is being influenced by LLMs

claims.claim: Nigerian and other British-colonial-educated English speakers use 'delve' as an ordinary word from school onward, so a single-word tell convicts entire human dialects.
claims.quote: no one used basic words like 'delve'
claims.page: Nigerians tackle American author for claiming 'delve' is only used by ChatGPT

claims.claim: Corpus analysis finds the 21 LLM focal words (delve, intricate, underscore, realm...) are probably not overrepresented in training data and not especially prevalent in any human English variety, undercutting the 'it's Nigerian English' defence while confirming the base-rate shift in LLM output is real and likely post-training.
claims.source: arXiv 2412.11385 — Juzek & Ward, Why Does ChatGPT 'Delve' So Much? (COLING 2025)
claims.quote: probably not overrepresented in the training data
claims.page: Sources of Lexical Overrepresentation in LLMs

claims.claim: Seven commercial detectors flagged 61.22% of 91 human-written TOEFL essays as AI (19.78% unanimously, 97.80% by at least one) while scoring near-perfectly on US 8th-grade essays, because they punish low-perplexity plain prose.
claims.source: arXiv 2304.02819 — Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou, 2023
claims.page: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers

claims.claim: A single 'employ literary language' self-edit prompt dropped detection of ChatGPT essays from up to 100% to up to 13% and of abstracts from 68% to 28%, so ornate prose evades detectors — the inverse of the folk tells.
claims.quote: detection rates dropping from up to 100% to up to 13%
claims.page: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers

claims.claim: Detectors learn that predictable word choice and simple sentences mean AI, so non-native writers' restricted vocabulary is misread as machine output.
claims.page: AI Detection Tools Falsely Accuse International Students of Cheating
